name: How do carpenters handle uneven walls and ceilings in older Denver homes?

mainEntity.name: How do carpenters handle uneven walls and ceilings in older Denver homes?

acceptedAnswer.text: In older Denver neighborhoods, houses often feature foundation settlement, sagging plaster, and wavy framing that make ceiling and floor lines uneven. Standard flat cuts will leave wide, unsightly gaps. Finish carpenters handle this by scribing the molding directly to the contour of the surface, using flexible backer materials, and coping inside corners rather than relying on standard 45-degree miter cuts. Paired with drywall patching and professional caulking, these finish carpentry methods keep trim lines visually straight despite irregular walls.
acceptedAnswer.description: Carpenters scribe profiles to uneven surfaces, hand-cope inside corners, and level out drywall dips to create tight, seamless joints on irregular surfaces.
